messages:
maria: monitoring-bot just opened an alert — sudden parity/error burst on PCIe lanes across rack-7 and rack-12, multiple GPUs reset. capacity down ~14% in us-west2. any immediate owners?
monitoring-bot: ALERT: pcie_parity_surge 
 - regions: us-west2
 - affected_racks: rack-7, rack-12
 - metric: gpu_xid_errors + thermal-CEA spikes
 - severity: high
kevin: on it. pulling logs now. do we know if this started after any deploys/firmware pushes?
maria: we pushed a small BIOS+BMC firmware to those racks at 04:12 UTC earlier today (rollout-2023-04-bios). rollout flag looked ok. ops timeline attached in pager duty.
aj: grabbing dmesg and nv-host logs from rack-7-node-0{3,4,5} — paste below.
```
[ 4021.234567] pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: Corrected error: type=Physical Layer, id=0000(Transmitter), severity=Corrected
[ 4021.234580] nvidia: Xid (PCIe CE) 31 on GPU 2
[ 4021.234590] kernel: pci_bus 0000:02: pcie error response: seu parity
[ 4022.009001] GPU-reset: GPU 2 reset due to parity error
```
ben: Xid 31 is often a PCIe link/soft CE cascade. Could be firmware regression or lane negotiation issue.
rachel: +1 on firmware suspicion — we had one vendor note about 'improved lane retrain' in that bundle. I recommended hold, but rollout continued.
kevin: plan suggestion: 1) immediately isolate and drain the worst hosts 2) roll back BIOS/BMC for the two racks to previous bundle 3) open vendor RMA for suspect cards if resets persist 4) enable additional telemetry (pcie AER counters) to validate. thoughts?
aj: agree. drain commands ready: `redwoodctl drain-host rack-7-node-04 --reason "pcie-parity-surge" --no-suspend-jobs`
maria: start drains for rack-7-node-03..05 and rack-12-node-01..02. mark as P1 so autoscaler can compensate.
sre-bot: Runbook link: https://internal/runbooks/pcie-parity-surge — recommends rollback for firmware if >10% of hosts affected.
ben: before rollback, can we confirm correlation matrix? i.e., all failures on hosts with bios v2.3.1? i'll run quick join.
kevin: yes run correlation. aj, can you grep inventory? `invctl list-hosts --filter bios=2.3.1 --format json | jq '.hosts | length'`
aj: quick check: 18 hosts running 2.3.1, 17 of them reported at least one parity CE in the last 30m. correlation strong.
rachel: ok initiate rollback plan. i'll prepare the rollback bundle and coordinate with oncall infra CI to limit blast radius.
maria: ops note: draining those hosts will temporarily reduce free GPUs — forecasted capacity after drains ~-22% baseline until we complete rollback or swap. product/infra-cost: we may need to burst on Dedicated for a few hours to keep SLOs. Eng-sre + product was pinged.
kevin: vendor open ticket: VEND-9872 created, sent logs and stack traces, asked for expedited RMA on cards showing repeated resets.
ben: short mitigation tweak to try in parallel: disable PCIe ASPM/l0s on those hosts to avoid aggressive power state transitions that can trigger retrain noise. small kernel cmdline: `pcie_aspm=off` — low risk but requires reboot.
aj: rebooting hosts for aspmdisable will disrupt jobs, prefer firmware rollback first.
kevin: agreed — do rollback first, if errors continue, enable aspmdisable on a canary and observe.
sre-bot: created incident INC-2023-0412-pcie-parity — assigned to eng-infra.
maria: owners: kevin -> drains + host coord, rachel -> rollback orchestration, aj -> logs + telemetry, ben -> vendor RMA follow-up. keep updates in this thread. :loud_sound:
kevin: starting drain now. posting progress.
maria: thanks everyone — will update execs and product on capacity impact and expected mitigation ETA. :thumbsup:
